title: Coast Guard warns of Chinese rocket debris in PH waters on Sept. 23 (Wed)
summary: MANILA, Philippines — The Coast Guard District (CGD) of Palawan warned vessels to steer clear of some coasts in the country on Wednesday, Sept. 23, due to potential debris that may fall during the…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Coast Guard District (CGD) of Palawan warned vessels to steer clear of some coasts in the country on Wednesday, Sept. 23, due to potential debris that may fall during the scheduled rocket launch by China.
The CGD cited the information issued by the Philippine Space Agency (PhilSa).
China’s Long March 8A rocket from Wenchang, Hainan is scheduled to conduct its launch between 9:24 p.m. and 10 p.m. (Philippine standard time) on Wednesday.
It warned that rocket debris may fall within the following identified drop zones:

items: 144 nautical miles from Bajo de Masinloc
190 nautical miles from El Nido, Palawan
46 nautical miles from Puerto Princesa, Palawan,
24 nautical miles from Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park
105 nautical miles from pangutaran Island, Sulu
117 nautical miles from Hadji Muhtamad, Basilan

blocks.text: The CGD advised all mariners, fishing vessels, passenger and cargo vessels, and those in the affected coastal communities to take precautionary measures during the launch period.
It also reminded the public not to touch, move or retrieve any suspected rocket debris or unfamiliar object found at sea or along the shoreline, as it may contain hazardous materials.
All debris or objects found must be reported to the Philippine Coast Guard or appropriate authorities, it added.

“The cooperation of all agencies concerned, local government units, maritime stakeholders, and the public is requested in ensuring the widest dissemination of this navigational warning,” the CGD Palawan said in a statement. /apl
